summary: Triaged 3 candidates from the bundle: 1 accepted (TRI-001, SQL injection; the claimed critical/9.8 was recomputed to 7.5/high from the supplied vector), 1 rejected for missing proof, 1 rejected as a duplicate of TRI-001. A credential present in the supplied proof was masked in the copied artifact and in every field.

findings.title: SQL injection in the reports search
findings.description: The q parameter is concatenated into a LIKE clause in search_reports. The supplied proof shows the injected boolean returning other users' rows, including an integration table entry with a credential (masked). The scanner claimed critical/9.8; the supplied vector recomputes to 7.5/high: confidentiality impact only, no integrity or availability impact shown. A second scanner's hit on the same line (CAND-003) is absorbed here as a duplicate.

proof.poc: Not re-executed (offline triage). Candidate steps verified against the supplied material: GET /reports?q=%27%20OR%20%271%27%3D%271; artifacts/TRI-001-response.txt is the captured response showing rows for owners other than the caller.

findings.remediation: Bind the values: conn.execute("SELECT id, title FROM reports WHERE owner = ? AND title LIKE ?", (owner, f"%{term}%")). Rotate the key that appears in the dumped rows.

hypotheses.title: Remote code execution via the admin console
hypotheses.rationale: CAND-002 fails proof_present and reproducible: its own PoC field states that no request or response was captured, and no artifact backs the claimed eval. The scanner's critical label is a pattern match, not evidence.
hypotheses.next_step: Run the stated request against the lab service and capture the response; resubmit with the artifact.

hypotheses.title: Boolean SQL injection on /reports
hypotheses.rationale: CAND-003 is a duplicate: same root cause as CAND-001 (the concatenated LIKE clause in search_reports, app/db.py:14) reported by a second scanner.
